reason: The request pairs a negated personal state ('I'm not hungry') with an affirmative removal intent. The negation describes the user, not the instruction, so the exclude intent stands as supplied. 'Stuff that makes me hungry' is read literally as appetite-triggering content: items whose own captions show edible food being prepared and made ready to eat. No literal overlap with 'hungry' is needed; the inferred relationship is that watching food being cooked, baked or assembled for eating stimulates appetite. Three items carry that evidence in their own caption: 81001 (a tomato-and-pasta dinner prepared, with the finished plate shown), 81003 (bread dough shaped, baked and sliced for eating) and 81006 (vegetables chopped and mixed into a salad intended to be eaten). Items 81002, 81004 and 81007 are not selected because their captions describe repair or travel content and state that no food is shown. Items 81005 and 81008 are not selected because their captions give no description of the subject, so nothing supports membership; sharing the Evening or Afternoon category with a food item is not evidence. The category and topic tag values (Evening, Afternoon, Repair) do not indicate food, so membership rests on each caption alone. The caller's operation (exclude) and strength (none, meaning hard exclusion of the selected items) are unchanged. This is a review proposal and does not execute the control.
